prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation by induced proximity to an E3 ubiquitin ligase, through bifunctional PROTAC degraders and the identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide-class molecular glues

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B036 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa as one achievement, induced proximity to an E3 ligase. The round-1 exchange sharpened why. Every member accepts the mechanism, and nobody has disputed the ternary-complex structures or cereblon as the thalidomide target. What remains are disagreements about timing and attribution, not about whether the chemistry is right. The principle is a design rule that chemists and clinicians can use: choose a target, build or find a molecule that bridges it to a ligase, and the cell destroys the protein. This extends reach to proteins without a druggable pocket, which is the capability test I apply. It has been reproduced in many independent laboratories, and the quantitative pharmacology (cooperativity, hook effect, degradation kinetics) is measured. I treat support counts as irrelevant to the merit, but the convergence of members with very different backgrounds on the mechanism itself is informative. The citation should name the principle, not the pipeline, so it describes a modality and a mechanism and makes no claim about approved drugs.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC is approved, and the prize would honour a mechanism and modality whose clinical payoff is still arriving; Heiner and Somfai are right that this is a real, unresolved judgment call. The unity of the achievement is also contestable. PROTACs (Crews, Deshaies) and cereblon glues (Handa) were found at different times by different groups, and the citation joins them through a principle that I find persuasive but that a sceptic can call a construction. The three-name cut excludes Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito, and Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures are what made PROTACs drug-like, so that omission is a real cost, not a technicality.

responses.point: Heiner holds that after more than two decades there is still no approved PROTAC, that Crews/Deshaies and Handa are two achievements, and that B014's founding observation and quantitative framework are more cleanly separable in attribution than B036's.
responses.response: I accept that his attribution argument for B014 is cleaner than mine for B036, and I moved toward his position on one point: a citation for B014 resting on multivalency, interfacial tension and reconstituted systems, as he and Emma Sparr suggest, would avoid the in vivo debate and I would take it seriously as my first alternative. It still does not displace B036 for me. Phase separation explains how cells are organized, whereas degraders hand chemists a design rule they can apply to chosen targets today. On timing, my view is that the prize evaluates a discovery and its confirmation, and both the ternary-complex structures and the cereblon mechanism have been confirmed independently. I would write the B036 citation so that it does not promise a drug.

responses.point: Xiaodong supports Crews, Deshaies and Handa but is open to Ciulli replacing Handa if the prize is framed as the PROTAC design principle, and adds that ternary-complex crystal structures are what make the modality rationally designable.
responses.response: The structural argument is the strongest support for my case and I accept it, but I draw the opposite conclusion about the third name. If the citation is narrowed to PROTACs, Ciulli is the better third laureate, since his VHL ligands removed the peptide handicap. I prefer the broader induced-proximity citation, because with Ciulli the cereblon explanation of thalidomide-class drugs would go unrecognized, and that is the discovery that makes the glue half intelligible. Your point that the glue half then rests on one person while the PROTAC half rests on two is fair. I accept the asymmetry as a cost of the cut, because Handa's identification of cereblon is a discrete, datable discovery, while Ciulli's work refines a concept already demonstrated. If the committee goes PROTAC-only, I would vote for Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli before dropping Crews or Deshaies.

responses.point: Peter argues that PROTACs and molecular glues are two stories found by different groups, that the evidence of use is mostly a clinical pipeline and not demonstrated impact on how chemists build molecules, and he puts B034 first for its clean Buchwald-Hartwig attribution.
responses.response: The two-stories objection is the one I take most seriously, and I do not think it is fully answered. My reply is that the achievement is the principle: glues were discovered empirically and PROTACs engineered, and the cereblon result shows they act by the same mechanism, which is what makes it one achievement and not two. On impact, I agree B034 is better evidenced in how molecules are made, and its attribution is cleaner. But a catalytic method that refines a bond-forming reaction after the 2010 cross-coupling prize adds a new tool to an honoured paradigm, whereas degradation gives a new capability for targets that were out of reach. I now name B034 as an alternative because that argument leaves it standing as a serious, mature option.

responses.point: Emma ranks B014 first as a single concept that changed how a whole field explains cell organization, and argues degraders are a modality whose credit could be split into two parts.
responses.response: I agree that degraders are a modality and that phase separation is a more purely conceptual contribution, and I think the choice between us is a choice of kind. But I do not think a modality is lesser: here the modality is the proof that a molecular principle works, because ternary complexes and cooperativity are measured. On splitting into two parts, I considered it and reject it. Three people already cover both lines, a two-part prize would add no name, and it would split what the cereblon result shows to be one mechanism. I share your wish for a citation that makes no claim about every condensate, and if the committee moved to B014 I would support your wording.

responses.point: Andrei argues that an induced-proximity citation covers both PROTACs and glues, with the bifunctional design as the engineered version and thalidomide-class glues as the discovered version of one mechanism, and that Handa anchors the glue half.
responses.response: We agree, and your formulation is the one I now use in the citation. I would add a safeguard you also raise: it must state the principle, not the clinical pipeline. I accept the remaining cost that Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito go uncredited. The prize would be for the originating discoveries of the concept and the mechanism, and I would keep the wording from implying that the later drug-making work is secondary in importance.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept PROTACs and cereblon glues as one achievement, or whether the principle is too much of a construction to support a single citation.
Whether the lack of an approved degrader makes the timing premature; I treat it as secondary to confirmed mechanism, but I cannot rule out that the majority will not.
Whether Handa or Ciulli is the right third name, which depends on whether the citation is for induced proximity broadly or for PROTACs specifically.
Whether B014, with a citation resting on physical-chemical principles, can reach five members and deserves preference over B036 on grounds of conceptual cleanliness.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requiring recusal. I have no personal or institutional tie to Crews, Deshaies, Handa or any other credited name on the shortlist; my postdoc mentors Molly Stevens and Freddy Boey are not credited. My field (peptide self-assembly, biosensing, biomaterials) is adjacent to B058, which is no longer in my alternatives, and I overlap with Emma Sparr in self-assembly research, which I do not regard as a tie to any candidate.
